At first, I thought it was just stress from juggling school and my shift work at the café—sometimes I’m on my feet for hours, and the noise from the espresso machine and customers doesn’t help. But lately, I’ve started noticing things… like smells. Out of nowhere, I’ll catch this strong scent of burnt hair, but no one else smells it. It happens when I’m alone, even at home.

And there are thoughts I can’t shake—like I’m meant for something much bigger than making lattes. Not just “I want a better job,” but like… I’m supposed to deliver some kind of message that only I can understand. People don’t get it, so I’ve stopped talking about it.

I don’t feel like myself. I cry a lot, skip classes, stay in bed—but not because I’m tired. It’s like nothing matters. Still, those thoughts and smells don’t seem to fade, even when I’m not feeling especially sad. Or maybe I’m always a little sad now—honestly, it’s hard to tell when it started or what came first.

I’ve been chosen to reveal truths no one else can see. I’ve started recording everything because my thoughts are too important to lose.

I admit, I’ve felt down sometimes—low energy, not wanting to get out of bed, wondering if any of it matters. That’s been coming and going for a few weeks here and there. But the smells and the mission—they’ve been constant, every single day. Even when I feel okay mood-wise, the voices and the smells don’t stop.
